distinctions_drawn: judgment of taste vs. judgment of the agreeable/good

objections_raised: disagreement between two observers under same conditions undermines universality
if everything can be beautiful, 'beauty' loses meaning

appeals_to_authority: Kant's texts (Critique of Judgment, Fundamental Principles)
named_thought_experiments: two people looking at Picasso painting

summary_of_core_decisions: The text reconstructs Kant's argument for subjective universality by chaining necessary conditions: disinterestedness → non-conceptual free play → universal communicability → subjective universality. It defends against objections by distinguishing universal validity from universal acceptance and by showing that disagreement stems from lack of disinterest. It draws implications: free play explains faculty harmony, any object can be judged beautiful, and aesthetic experience bridges the phenomenal/noumenal gap.
